description: The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) publishes an Annual Safety Review (ASR) that gives an overview of aviation safety in Europe for the past year, compares it with the previous ten years, analyses accidents and serious incidents across all aviation domains and feeds the European Plan for Aviation Safety (EPAS). The 2025 edition (26 August 2025) covers 2024, when European traffic passed 7.7 million flights; it counts 14 fatal airline accidents worldwide with 304 fatalities, 3 fatal accidents in European commercial air transport, and fatal accidents in general aviation, helicopters, balloons and sailplanes, with none for drones. Its ten chapters cover the safety overview, aeroplanes, helicopters, balloons, sailplanes, unmanned aircraft systems, aerodromes and ground handling, air traffic management and air navigation services, occurrence reporting and the European Risk Classification Scheme, and standardisation. Coverage: EASA member states, with global context for airline accidents; annual editions. Format and access: PDF report (about 5.3 MB) and an appendix listing fatal accidents (PDF); free. Licence: EASA reuse terms were not read. Caveats: figures are aggregated in PDF tables, not an open dataset; occurrence-level data are not published here. The same site also hosts the aerodromes rulebook (Regulation (EU) No 139/2014) and environmental databases, which were not read for this record. Simulation uses: accident and incident baselines by domain for aviation and airport risk and emergency planning. Related records: the FAA ASIAS public safety data (data-faa-asias-aviation-safety-data) is the United States counterpart.
